extracted.intended_audience: researchers, evaluators, and practitioners of science communication and public engagement (including institutional program designers, policymakers, and funders)
extracted.subtask_description: A curated listing of AAAS research and reports about best practices, evaluation frameworks, measurement scales, and guidance for communicating science to the public and to policymakers. Useful for researchers designing engagement programs, evaluators measuring outcomes, and practitioners informing policy-facing communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication Best Practices (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: A body of research/guidance on effective approaches to science communication and public engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes works on inclusive engagement, foundational skills frameworks, strategic environmental communication, bridging theory and practice, public attitudes, and typologies for engagement. Serves as an umbrella for studies that identify recommended practices and skills for communicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Institutions Should Support Inclusive Engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions should actively support inclusive public engagement approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflections on the AAAS Center for Public Engagement approach (Kimbrell et al., 2022) arguing for institutional structures and practices that enable inclusive engagement with diverse publics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundational Skills for Science Communication: A Preliminary Framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed framework identifying foundational skills needed for effective science communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a preliminary taxonomy of skills communicators should develop; intended to guide training and program design (Aurbach et al., 2019; white paper co-published by AAAS and partners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Science Communication on Environmental Issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on designing strategic communication tailored to environmental topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes framing, audience analysis, and strategy choices specific to environmental issues (Nisbet & Markowitz, 2016). Useful for program design and assessing appropriateness of communication strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science communication research: bridging theory and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Work connecting theoretical insights with practical communication activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses how research can inform practice and vice versa; helps evaluators and practitioners translate evidence into actionable engagement methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Americans' attitudes about science and technology: the social context for public communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Research describing public attitudes that form the context for communication efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides evidence on public opinion and social context which should inform message design, targeting, and evaluation of communication impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typology for public engagement with science
rubrics_metrics.description: A conceptual framework/typology for categorizing public engagement activities involving scientists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers a classification system for engagement types to help designers and evaluators differentiate goals, methods, and appropriate measures (Storksdieck et al., 2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement research and major approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey of major approaches to public engagement with science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes prevailing approaches (e.g., deficit model, dialogue, participatory) to inform selection of engagement modalities and evaluation approaches (Nisbet & Markowitz, 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public engagement with and communication of science in a web-2.0 media environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on communicating science in interactive, social-media-rich environments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses implications of Web 2.0 platforms for engagement strategies, audience behaviors, and evaluation metrics (Yeo, 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluating Public Engagement (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and frameworks focused on assessing outcomes and effectiveness of public engagement efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes landscape reviews, case studies, measurement scale development (outcome expectations, self-efficacy), and formative evaluation frameworks to guide program design and impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: AAAS Civic Science Fellowship Project — formative evaluation framework
rubrics_metrics.description: A formative framework to evaluate civic science efforts developed from a landscape review and case studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informed by a landscape review of relationship-building approaches on climate resilience and three in-depth case studies; intended to evaluate future civic science efforts and design initial civic science experiments for culture change at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landscape Report of Relationship-Building for Climate Resilience Collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: A landscape report that snapshots existing relationship-building approaches and identifies thematic challenges for local engagement on climate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies typographies/streams of public engagement on climate and provides recommendations for subject-matter experts, funders/institutions, and evaluators/researchers; useful as a diagnostic tool for program planners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case studies of flood resilience and recovery networks (rural Midwest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Case analyses of relationship-building among community members, organizations, SMEs, universities, and civic groups in three small-town flood resilience/recovery networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compares engagement activities under different organizational auspices (university-affiliated, grassroots, civic nonprofit) and provides insights for public engagement with rural communities on climate-related issues; useful for contextualized evaluation and transferability assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome expectations scale for scientists (assessing public engagement outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: A measurement scale to assess scientists' expectations about the outcomes of public engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes snapshot and technical reports that offer a validated instrument for measuring expected outcomes, which can be used in program evaluation and research on motivations and perceived impacts (Peterman et al., 2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-efficacy for public engagement scale (validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A validated scale that measures scientists’ self-efficacy for engaging with the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides both snapshot and technical reports detailing scale validation, enabling evaluators to measure confidence and capability among scientists to perform engagement activities (Robertson Evia et al., 2017).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientists’ prioritization of communication objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures which communication objectives scientists prioritize when engaging the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical findings (Besley & Dudo, 2016) inform program design and evaluation by revealing which goals (e.g., education, persuasion, trust-building) are emphasized by scientists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientists' views about communication training
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on scientists’ perspectives regarding the value and content of communication training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers evidence on training needs, uptake, and perceived benefits that can guide development and assessment of training programs (Besley, Dudo & Storksdieck, 2015).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientists' perceptions of the public and online engagement behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of what scientists think about the public and how those beliefs relate to their online engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Findings inform expectations about who engages online, motivations, and potential barriers or facilitators of online public communication (Besley, 2014).

rubrics_metrics.name: Science in Policymaking (category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research and guidance on how scientific information is communicated to and used by policymakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers factors affecting use of science in Congress, barriers, credibility dimensions (e.g., perceived bias), recommended practices, and evidence-based communication strategies for policy contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicating Science to Congress — factors affecting use
rubrics_metrics.description: Study examining factors that affect how scientific information is used in personal offices of members of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on workshops, interviews, and surveys of legislative staff to map opportunities and barriers, the interplay of scientific knowledge with behavior/experience/culture, and the nature of scientist–policymaker interactions; informs how to tailor communication to legislative contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barriers in communicating science for policy in Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of obstacles to effective communication of science within legislative contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference proceedings and studies that document structural, cultural, and informational barriers and suggest areas for institutional or communicative change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived bias as a dimension of credibility with policymakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Perceived bias is identified as a key component shaping credibility when communicating science with policymakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research (Akerlof et al., 2018) highlights that perceived bias affects whether policymakers find scientific information credible and thus usable; suggests credibility assessments should include perceived bias measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congress's Use of Science: Considerations for Science Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for science organizations on promoting the use of evidence in policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical considerations (AAAS 2017; updated 2019) for organizations seeking to increase evidence uptake, including relationship-building, timing, and presentation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-based science communications with policymakers (best practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of best practices for presenting scientific information to policymakers, derived from integrated literature, surveys, case studies and interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available through American University; synthesizes empirically grounded recommendations for how to communicate evidence effectively in policymaking contexts (project led by Suhay et al.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended Practices for Science Communication with Policymakers (guide)
rubrics_metrics.description: A guide that recommends specific practices for communicating science to policymakers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes concrete recommendations and possibly checklists or templates to improve the chances that scientific evidence will be considered in policy decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentives, Opportunities, and Success? AAAS Members’ Experiences Communicating with Policymakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Research exploring AAAS members’ experiences and the incentives/opportunities that shape scientists’ policy engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides empirical insight into what enables or discourages scientists from engaging with policymakers and can inform program and institutional incentive structures.
